title: Multi-Active-S-Box Bias in 7-Round DES Differential-Linear Distinguishers
summary: Maximum bias is verified for 7-round DES differential-linear distinguishers with one active S-box at each end; whether multi-active-S-box cases can exceed it, even with subcipher dependency, remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: For $7$-round $\mathrm{DES}$ differential-linear distinguishers, a maximum-bias distinguisher has been verified within the class that starts and ends with a single active S-box. Determine whether any distinguisher with more than one active S-box in its input difference or output bias can exceed that verified maximum, including one that exploits dependency between the subciphers.

scope.domain: This is a differential-linear cryptanalysis problem about the bias of 7-round DES distinguishers and active S-box patterns.
parameters: 7 rounds: the round count for the DES distinguisher
active S-box count: the number in the input difference or output bias
distinguisher bias: the quantity compared against the verified maximum
subcipher dependency: a dependency that a candidate distinguisher may exploit
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether a 7-round DES differential-linear distinguisher with more than one active S-box in its input difference or output bias can exceed the verified maximum, including when it exploits dependency between the subciphers.

citations.label: DLCT: A New Tool for Differential-Linear Cryptanalysis

progress.summary: The source reports maximal bias within the class of 7-round distinguishers that starts and ends with a single active S-box. It presents the unchecked multi-active-S-box case as highly unlikely to exceed that bias, even when subcipher dependency is exploited.
citation_labels: Achiya Bar-On et al., DLCT: A New Tool for Differential-Linear Cryptanalysis
